Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Branch: feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches (four prior commits landed: 9f46912, ab04241, 6631e05, b16298e — all committed, do not touch). This is SFCC-91 Step 4 of 4, the final step: wiring the already-built `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` into the real PDP page. Current changes are uncommitted in `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` only — do not commit, do not stage. Test it and report findings — you never fix anything.

Read `git diff -- overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` yourself first. The change is small: one import, and one new `renderVariationAttribute` prop on the main `<ProductView>` call site (previously line ~891, now ~894 after the import addition):

```tsx
renderVariationAttribute={(attr) =>
  attr.id === 'color' ? (
    <ZimmColourSwatchGroup
      label={attr.name ?? ''}
      selectedName={attr.selectedValue?.name}
      selectedValue={attr.selectedValue?.value}
      values={attr.values.map((v) => ({
        value: v.value ?? '',
        name: v.name,
        href: v.href,
        imageUrl: v.image?.disBaseLink || v.image?.link,
      }))}
    />
  ) : undefined
}
```

## What to verify

1. **Type coercions.** `attr.name ?? ''` and `v.value ?? ''` exist because `SfccVariationAttribute.name` and `SfccVariationValue.value` (defined in `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` around lines 98-107) are typed optional, while `ZimmColourSwatchGroupProps.label` and `ZimmColourSwatchValue.value` (defined in `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` around lines 44-72) require non-optional `string`. Read both type definitions yourself and confirm this is accurate — the coercions are a real typing necessity, not decorative. Then think about whether an empty-string fallback could ever produce a genuinely wrong (not just theoretically-possible) result with real SFCC data — I already checked this against the live dev Commerce API earlier this build and confirmed a real colour attribute always carries both `name` and `value`, so this should be a type-safety-only fallback with no practical failure mode; verify my reasoning rather than just repeating it, and flag it if you find a case where it matters.

2. **The `imageUrl` fallback chain** (`v.image?.disBaseLink || v.image?.link`). Confirm this matches base SFCC's own `getVariantValueSwatch` resolution (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-attributes.js`) — same fallback shape, so a colour with no `disBaseLink` but a real `link` still resolves, and a colour with neither correctly resolves to `undefined`, which is exactly the signal `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s own AC-5 filter (already built in Step 3) needs to exclude that colour.

3. **`attr.id === 'color'`** — confirm this is genuinely the correct literal to check against (not `'colour'`, not case-sensitive-wrong) by cross-referencing against how `product-view/index.tsx`'s own `renderDefaultVariationAttribute` (the extracted base rendering, built in Step 1) uses the identical `id === 'color'` check for its swatch-vs-square shape decision — they must agree, since both are reading the same SFCC attribute id.

4. **Scope discipline on the set/bundle instances.** The two other `<ProductView>` call sites (now at lines ~804 and ~830) were explicitly left untouched. Read the surrounding context of BOTH to understand what they actually render — are these genuinely a different case (e.g. read-only child-product summaries with no interactive variation selection at all), or could skipping them create a visibly inconsistent experience (e.g. a bundle/set page showing base-SFCC unstyled square swatches for colour right next to the main product's newly-styled circular image swatches)? Read enough of the surrounding bundle/set rendering logic to give a real, evidence-based answer, not a guess — if you find these two instances don't even reach the `variationAttributes` rendering path at all (e.g. they render a fixed/pre-selected child product with no picker), that confirms the plan's "different layout, out of scope" reasoning; if they DO render a live colour picker, flag this as a real, visible inconsistency for a future story rather than silently agreeing it's fine.

5. **No hook touched.** Grep the diff and confirm zero changes to any `use-*` hook file.

6. **Gates**, reproduced yourself:
```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npm run test
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```
Current baseline on this branch (verified directly moments ago, not estimated): tsc 0 errors; test 28 files/432 tests all passing (this step adds no test file); lint 20 problems (4 pre-existing errors in routes.tsx:23,24 and recipeGuards.test.ts:116,335, 16 warnings), exit 1; audit:tokens exactly 4 unacknowledged (header/index.tsx, header.ts x2, navConstants.ts)/22 acknowledged, exit 1. Confirm none of these numbers moved and nothing new appears attributable to `product-detail/index.tsx`.

## A test file genuinely does not exist for this page — is that actually fine here?

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` has no dedicated `.test.tsx` (confirmed: it's a ~900-line page with heavy data-fetching hook dependencies — `useProduct`, `useCurrentBasket`, etc. — that would need extensive mocking to render at all). The plan explicitly does not ask for a new test file at this step, deferring verification to a real dev-server visual check instead. Independently judge whether this is a reasonable call for JUST this specific 18-line addition (pure JSX composition + data mapping, zero new branching logic of its own — all real logic already lives in, and is already tested by, `ZimmColourSwatchGroup` itself) or whether you think a narrow, targeted test would be cheap enough to be worth suggesting anyway despite the plan not requiring it. If you think a test is genuinely warranted, don't write one yourself (not your job) — just say so as a finding.

## What Vitest structurally cannot prove here — say so plainly, don't overclaim

AC 4 (clicking a colour swatch updates the URL without a full page reload) cannot be verified by anything you can run — it requires an actual browser navigating an actual PDP against real product data, which is exactly why the plan defers this specific step's final check to Marcel's own running dev server rather than an automated gate. Do not attempt to fabricate or approximate this proof; state clearly that this remains unverified by any automated means and is the one thing a human must confirm.

Report in the standard format: CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/UNSUPPORTED, UNIFORM/ONE-OFF. State explicitly what you tried to falsify and could not, and what you could not verify at all (and why). Do not fix anything — only report.

8	import {useMemo} from 'react'
9	import {useLocation} from 'react-router-dom'
10	
11	// Other Hooks
12	import {useVariationParams} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-params'
13	
14	// Utils
15	import {updateSearchParams} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url'
16	import {usePDPSearchParams} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-pdp-search-params'
17	import {filterImageGroups} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils'
18	/**
19	 * Return the first image in the `swatch` type image group for a given
20	 * variation value of a product.
21	 *
22	 * @param {Object} product
23	 * @param {Object} variationValue
24	 * @returns {Object} image
25	 */
26	export const getVariantValueSwatch = (product, variationValue) => {
27	    const {imageGroups = []} = product
28	
29	    return filterImageGroups(imageGroups, {
30	        viewType: 'swatch',
31	        variationValues: {
32	            ['color']: variationValue.value
33	        }
34	    })?.[0]?.images?.[0]
35	}
36	
37	/**
38	 * Build a product href
39	 *
40	 * @param {Object} product
41	 * @param {Object} params
42	 * @param {Object} location
43	 * @returns {String} a product url for the current variation value.
44	 */
45	export const buildVariantValueHref = ({
46	    pathname,
47	    existingParams,
48	    newParams,
49	    productId,
50	    isProductPartOfSet,
51	    isProductPartOfBundle
52	}) => {
53	    const [allParams, productParams] = existingParams
54	
55	    if (isProductPartOfSet || isProductPartOfBundle) {
56	        updateSearchParams(productParams, newParams)
57	        allParams.set(productId, productParams.toString())
58	    } else {
59	        updateSearchParams(allParams, newParams)
60	    }
61	
62	    return `${pathname}?${allParams.toString()}`
63	}
64	
65	/**
66	 * Determine if a products variant attribute value is orderable without having to
67	 * load the variant in question, but filtering the list of variants with the
68	 * passed in attribute values.
69	 *
70	 * @param {Object} product
71	 * @param {Object} variationParams
72	 * @returns
73	 */
74	export const isVariantValueOrderable = (product, variationParams) => {
75	    return product.variants
76	        .filter(({variationValues}) =>
77	            Object.keys(variationParams).every(
78	                (key) => variationValues[key] === variationParams[key]
79	            )
80	        )
81	        .some(({orderable}) => orderable)
82	}
83	
84	/**
85	 * Use a decorated version of a product variation attributes. This version
86	 * will have the following additions: which variation attribute is selected,
87	 * each value will have a product url, the swatch image if there is one, and
88	 * an updated orderable flag.
89	 *
90	 * @param {Object} product
91	 * @param {boolean} isProductPartOfSet
92	 * @param {boolean} isProductPartOfBundle
93	 * @param {Object} controlledVariationValues - Optional controlled variation values (skips URL reading)
94	 * @param {Function} onVariationChange - Optional callback for controlled mode (attributeId, value) => void
95	 * @returns {Array} a decorated variation attributes list.
96	 *
97	 */
98	export const useVariationAttributes = (
99	    product = {},
100	    isProductPartOfSet = false,
101	    isProductPartOfBundle = false,
102	    controlledVariationValues = null,
103	    onVariationChange = null
104	) => {
105	    const {variationAttributes = []} = product
106	    const location = useLocation()
107	    const variationParams = useVariationParams(
108	        product,
109	        isProductPartOfSet,
110	        isProductPartOfBundle,
111	        controlledVariationValues
112	    )
113	    const existingParams = usePDPSearchParams(product.id)
114	    const isBundleChildVariant = isProductPartOfBundle && product?.type?.variant
115	
116	    // In the product bundle edit modal on the cart page, the variant ID of each bundle child is used as a key
117	    // for query parameters, so when a new variant is selected, a new query parameter is added since variants
118	    // have different IDs. The old one is not overwritten with existing logic so we remove it here
119	    if (isBundleChildVariant && !controlledVariationValues) {
120	        const [allParams] = existingParams
121	        product?.variants?.forEach(({productId: variantId}) => {
122	            if (variantId !== product.id && allParams.get(variantId)) {
123	                allParams.delete(variantId)
124	            }
125	        })
126	    }
127	
128	    // In controlled mode, we don't depend on location.search
129	    const isControlled = controlledVariationValues !== null
130	    const memoKey = isControlled ? product : [location.search, product]
131	
132	    return useMemo(
133	        () =>
134	            variationAttributes.map((variationAttribute) => ({
135	                ...variationAttribute,
136	                selectedValue: {
137	                    name: variationAttribute.values.find(
138	                        ({value}) => value === variationParams?.[variationAttribute.id]
139	                    )?.name,
140	                    value: variationParams?.[variationAttribute.id]
141	                },
142	                values: variationAttribute.values.map((value) => {
143	                    const params = {
144	                        ...variationParams,
145	                        [variationAttribute.id]: value.value
146	                    }
147	
148	                    return {
149	                        ...value,
150	                        image: getVariantValueSwatch(product, value),
151	                        // In controlled mode, don't provide href (use callback instead)
152	                        href: isControlled
153	                            ? null
154	                            : buildVariantValueHref({
155	                                  pathname: location.pathname,
156	                                  existingParams,
157	                                  newParams: params,
158	                                  productId: product.id,
159	                                  isProductPartOfSet,
160	                                  isProductPartOfBundle
161	                              }),
162	                        orderable: isVariantValueOrderable(product, params)
163	                    }
164	                })
165	            })),
166	        Array.isArray(memoKey) ? memoKey : [memoKey]
167	    )
168	}
